source: Yahoo Finance delayed adjusted NIFTY 50 price-index history (^NSEI); same-calendar-day bars excluded
name: Risk-budgeted trend
formula: weekly_target = I(EMA15 > EMA45) * min(1, 8% / max(EWMA21 annualized SD, rolling63 annualized SD))

assumptions.execution: Signal after close t; execute at close t+1; first new-position return is t+1 to t+2
assumptions.dividends: Excluded because Yahoo ^NSEI is a price index
assumptions.taxes_and_market_impact: Excluded; cost stress is shown separately
assumptions.daily_bar_policy: Only sessions dated before the current Asia/Kolkata calendar date are accepted
assumptions.partial_week_policy: A current partial W-FRI period cannot create a rebalance

cross_market.frozen_parameters: 15/45 EMA regime, max(21-session EWMA, 63-session rolling) risk forecast, 8% target, weekly completed-period decisions, 10 bps one-way cost

promotion_gates.gate: Historical maximum drawdown no worse than 20%
Positive Sharpe at double base cost
Selection-adjusted Deflated Sharpe probability at least 95%
95% paired-bootstrap lower bound for Sharpe edge over volatility-only above zero
Frozen Sharpe transfer wins in at least four of six Indian indices
At least 252 genuinely unseen forward sessions

verdict.headline: Defensive risk control, not demonstrated alpha
verdict.reason: The rule reduces historical drawdown, but selection-aware uncertainty, volatility-only controls, transfer tests, and the lack of unseen forward data prevent a production trading claim.

references.title: Time Series Momentum — Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen
Volatility Managed Portfolios — Moreira and Muir
The Stationary Bootstrap — Politis and Romano
The Deflated Sharpe Ratio — Bailey and Lopez de Prado
A Simple, Positive Semi-definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix — Newey and West
On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios — Cederburg et al.

limitations: The NIFTY 50 price index is not directly tradable and excludes dividends.
Cash earns zero; actual cash yield, financing, taxes, impact, and ETF tracking error are omitted.
The same history informed many earlier and current variants, so it is not a pristine holdout.
The rule is long/cash only and can miss fast rebounds or lose before a weekly exit executes.
Maximum drawdown is one path-dependent historical extreme, not a promised future limit.
A total-return instrument and a prospectively logged paper test are required before live use.
